title: Three Rules for Better Simple Sandwiches (Pan Bagnat Demonstration)
summary: This video reframes everyday, simple sandwiches as a trio of guiding concepts—bread treatment, flavor and texture contrast, and thoughtful assembly—then demonstrates how to apply them through a pan Bagnat-inspired tuna sandwich. It covers practical bread prep (toasting, optional interior removal to create a bread trough, and oiling), building a richly seasoned olive salad with tuna, tomatoes, and hard-cooked eggs, and the importance of pressing a filled sandwich to hold its shape. The host extends the lessons with two additional builds (turkey on ciabatta with kimchi and avocado; egg salad on rye with radishes and pickles) to illustrate how bread choice, fillings, and contrasts influence results. The video also provides appendices on make-ahead components (pickled avocado, Dijonnaise, sumac onions) and assembly tactics to prevent sogginess or fillings from slipping, capped with a sponge-based demonstration of waterproofing bread. Across sections, the content emphasizes planning, texture/flavor balance, and deliberate layering to improve even simple sandwiches.

sections.title: Core sandwich concepts
sections.description: Introductory framing of three practical concepts the host uses to improve simple sandwiches: how bread is treated, how contrasting textures and flavors are paired, and how the sandwich is assembled.

sections.title: Pan Bagnat: bread, oil, olive salad, and pressing
sections.description: Demonstrates Andrew Janjigian’s pan bagnat: hollowed baguette bottom, toasted and brushed with extra-virgin olive oil, layered with an olive salad (nicoise olives, red onions, capers, anchovies, Dijon, herbs), tuna, tomato, hard-cooked egg, and the remaining olive salad; wrapped and pressed for at least an hour.

sections.title: Bread handling: toast, no toast, and griddling
sections.description: Explains how bread handling affects moisture and structure: when to toast, the option to griddle stale bread for extra dry surface and richness, and using interior-removal to form a trough for fillings.

sections.title: Filling principles and contrast
sections.description: Outlines how fillings should be seasoned and how contrast in texture and flavor (chew vs tenderness, crisp vs juicy, savory vs pungent) guides ingredient selection and composition.

sections.title: Turkey on ciabatta with kimchi and avocado
sections.description: A concrete example pairing ciabatta with turkey, kimchi, and avocado to create a sandwich with contrasting textures and a punchy, spicy-sour profile.

sections.title: Egg salad on rye: radishes and pickles
sections.description: Demonstrates an egg-salad build on rye with radishes and pickles to add crunch and acidity, countering richness and maintaining interest across bites.

sections.title: Make-ahead sandwich components: pickled avocado, Dijonnaise, sumac onions
sections.description: Introduces three versatile components to speed assembly and broaden flavor options: pickled avocado, a prepared Dijonnaise, and bright sumac onions.

sections.title: Assembly pitfalls and fixes
sections.description: Identifies common problems (bread sogginess and fillings slipping) and offers strategies: toast or oil the bottom slice to prevent soggy bread, create troughs, place grippy ingredients between slippery ones, and wrap if needed for eating.

sections.title: Takeaways and next steps
sections.description: Encourages thoughtful ingredient selection and methodical assembly as a path to consistently better sandwiches, ending with a call to subscribe and explore further resources.
